inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement share-based compensation add-back $61.7M plus $12.5M taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards (financing activities); STERIS publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. Same basis applied to FY2021/FY2023 for the owner-FCF CAGRs.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares, Q1 FY2027 10-Q (quarter to 2026-06-30), 97.9M. Held FLAT because SBC (incl. equity-award taxes) is fully expensed in the flows. STERIS is a funded repurchaser: FY2026 repurchases $235.5M and Q1 FY2027 $115.5M (both incl. award-tax withholding), well above the SBC charge, so the flat count is paid for in cash.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), beta ~0.85 (defensive healthcare consumables/services), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~8.6%. Debt ~$1.9B against ~$20.5B market cap (~8.5% weight) at ~4.5% pre-tax / ~3.5% after tax -> WACC ~8.2%; rounded up to 8.5% for the capital-equipment cyclicality inside Healthcare. Same WACC in every scenario -- risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not a stacked premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating-lease cost sits inside operating income/EBITDA, so leases are charged in the flows; operating-lease liabilities are NOT in net debt (one treatment).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: infection-prevention consumables, service, capital equipment, contract sterilization AST and Life Sciences). Routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md; first valuation of STE (no memory entry). Irish plc but US-domiciled operations, USD statements and USD NYSE quote, so the non-US adaptations do not apply. D&A path is DEPRECIATION ONLY (FY26 $218.3M = 3.7% of revenue): the $268.2M amortization of acquired intangibles (mostly Cantel, 2021) is excluded so EBIT here is EBITA, and the cash-tax rate is calibrated to that base (FY26 cash taxes $289.0M / EBITA ~$1,370M = 21.1%; ~22% unlevered after adding back the interest shield). This avoids a perpetual tax shield from book-only amortization. Adjusted EBITDA = GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC (FY26 $1,650.0M, 27.8%); GAAP OI still carries restructuring/acquisition costs, so the margin base is slightly conservative. Net debt at 2026-06-30 = long-term debt $1,650.2M + short-term borrowings $243.4M - cash $482.3M (the CSV TotalDebt column omits the short-term borrowings). Working capital capture negative (-8% of the revenue increase): receivables and inventory exceed payables in a capital-equipment/consumables manufacturer. Interest income not stripped (net debt, not net cash). Revenue CAGRs are inflated by the Cantel acquisition (closed June 2021, paid largely in stock) and depressed by the Dental divestiture; the forward path is anchored to organic growth (FY26 +8.7% reported, Q1 FY27 +7.3% YoY). No Analysis.json existed at build time, so narratives are drawn from the filings and business profile. FY2027 numeric guidance was not in the extracted data; year-1 growth is anchored to Q1 FY27 run-rate.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 5.7% diverges >30% from revenue 3yr CAGR 9.4%; 5yr equity/revenue CAGRs (13.1%/13.8%) are inflated by the stock-funded Cantel acquisition (FY2022). EPS 3yr CAGR omitted: FY2023 GAAP EPS $1.07 is depressed by a ~$490M goodwill impairment (Q2 FY23), making it meaningless.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes): FY2021 $414.8M, FY2023 $342.5M, FY2026 $898.2M. The 3yr figure starts from a FY2023 trough (Cantel integration, supply-chain inventory build, high capex) and is not a forward rate. Owner-FCF CAGR is close to reported, so SBC is not growing faster than cash flow (SBC ~1.0-1.3% of revenue).

base.narrative: Organic growth decelerates from the Q1 FY27 ~7% run-rate to GDP+ by year 9; procedure-volume-driven consumables and service plus AST/Life Sciences recovery hold mid-single digits. Margin expands ~2pp on pricing, mix toward recurring revenue and Cantel synergies; capex eases from the AST capacity build. Global minimum tax nudges the cash rate to 23%.

bull.narrative: Bioprocessing/pharma restocking and med-device outsourcing drive AST and Life Sciences to high-single-digit growth, hospital capital equipment replacement cycle stays strong, and EtO-to-radiation (gamma/X-ray/E-beam) modality shift favours STERIS's installed network. Operating leverage takes adjusted EBITDA margin to ~31.5%.

bear.narrative: Hospital capital budgets tighten and procedure growth normalises; EPA ethylene-oxide emission rules and litigation raise AST compliance cost and force capex; tariffs on imported components and consumables compress margins; Cantel endoscopy franchise loses share to single-use scopes. Growth slips to low single digits and margin erodes ~1pp; Irish/Pillar Two tax changes lift the cash rate.

scenario_narratives.base: STERIS keeps compounding as a recurring-revenue infection-prevention franchise (consumables + service ~70% of revenue): surgical procedure volumes drive Healthcare consumables and service, AST contract sterilization grows with med-device volumes, Life Sciences recovers from the post-COVID bioprocessing destock. Organic growth fades from ~7% to 3%; margins expand ~2pp from pricing and mix; capex normalises after the AST capacity programme.
scenario_narratives.bull: The radiation-modality shift away from ethylene oxide and med-device outsourcing make AST a high-single-digit grower with pricing power, bioprocessing restocking lifts Life Sciences, and the hospital capital-equipment replacement backlog persists. Growth stays 6-8% for five years and adjusted EBITDA margin reaches ~31.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The axes turn against it at once: EPA EtO rules and Willowbrook-style litigation raise AST cost, US hospital capex budgets are cut as Medicaid funding tightens, tariffs squeeze consumable margins, and single-use endoscopes erode the Cantel reprocessing franchise. Growth slips to 2.5-4% and margin falls to 27%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): EtO regulatory/litigation exposure in AST and hospital-capex/tariff sensitivity are live, though the balance sheet (net debt ~0.9x EBITDA) carries no solvency risk. Base 55%: a defensive, mostly recurring revenue base with a long record of mid-to-high single-digit organic growth makes the central path the most likely. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs AST modality share gains, a Life Sciences rebound and sustained hospital capex simultaneously.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF view of a mature infection-prevention compounder: SBC and equity-award taxes expensed, share count flat (funded by buybacks), EBITA-based tax so book amortization of Cantel intangibles creates no phantom shield, and a terminal cap of 18x base so the value does not lean on a Gordon multiple the market need not grant.
key_risks_to_valuation: Ethylene-oxide regulation and litigation in Applied Sterilization Technologies
Hospital capital-equipment budget cycle and US healthcare funding changes
Tariffs on imported components/consumables compressing margin
Single-use endoscope substitution eroding the Cantel reprocessing franchise
Terminal value ~60% of EV; value is sensitive to the 8.5% WACC and 18x cap
